html:
SMTO-EXE-0034 — SMTO's data step tried to use a tool it isn't allowed

GUID: d3d9e027-dc8a-41f4-b686-206cf346e8df
Slug: transform-import-unsupported
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO's quick data calculation tried to use something beyond simple data handling, such as files or the internet. For safety, that kind of step can only work with data. Nothing was run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Wait a moment and watch the task. SMTO usually rewrites the calculation using only the data tools it is allowed. This refusal is reported back to SMTO so it can choose an allowed approach.
  2. If the work really needs files or the internet, ask SMTO in the conversation to do that part as its own step, such as running a command on a Gateway. Those steps go through your normal permissions and approvals instead of the data-only step.

What success looks like

  • The step completes, or the task continues with a separate step that you approved.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't switch off the data-only safety check in the Agent Checks menu just to make this step pass; it keeps quick calculations away from your files and network.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The data-only python.transform sandbox import hook rejected a relative import or a module outside its allowlist (collections, csv, datetime, decimal, fractions, functools, html, itertools, json, math, operator, re, statistics, textwrap).

What this means

  • The transform sandbox's import hook rejected a relative import or a module outside its supported data-only module set. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • The transform sandbox's import hook rejected a relative import or a module outside its supported data-only module set.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the requested import with the sandbox's supported modules and whether the task actually requires external execution.

How to fix it

  • Rewrite the transform to use only the allowlisted modules (agent_runtime.execution.transform_worker.data_importer). If file, process or network access is genuinely needed and authorized, use the explicit Python or Shell execution capability instead; do not disable the execution.transform_sandbox check to get past this.
  • Use supported transformation modules, or use the explicit Python execution capability when external operations are intended and authorized.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The transformation uses permitted data modules, or separately authorized work uses the explicit Python execution capability.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
